## 9.5 Anti-loophole rules: why powers don't break finance

> CANON: Every obvious scheme has been tried. Every one fails on at least one hard rule. The following are settled doctrine, taught to every threshold-agency recruit and every Argent Vault compliance officer:

**Conjured gold / conjured anything of value.**
Fails on [02_WORLD_RULES.md](02_WORLD_RULES.md) I & II: *borrowed matter reverts within 72 hours*. Financial settlement clears on T+2 at the fastest; by the time the receiving bank's assay finishes, the gold is gone â€” sometimes *during* the assay, which is how the 2009 "Zurich reversion" was discovered (three vault officers, early retirement, generous pensions, no public record). Attempting this at scale is also Seismograph-visible (02, II). Verdict: *works once, badly, then you're famous and poor.*

**Precognition trading.**
Fails on economics and Erosion. Financial-precognition Resonances exist at small scales (02, II) â€” and every major exchange runs Lantern-screened compliance: listed-company news flows are monitored for Tide-pressure signatures, and "impossibly lucky" traders are investigated by people who know what Erosion looks like.

> CANON: **What a precog actually perceives.** The Undertow has no time (02, I) â€” so precognition does not "see the future." It reads **present informational traces and probability branches**: order-book pressure, the informational wake of decisions already made but not yet announced, the shape of the adjacent possible. **Observer reflexivity** is the binding constraint: the more observers price in a branch, the faster the branch decays â€” a precog trading *against* a market they can see is sawing the branch they're standing on. Edge is therefore self-limiting: it works small, briefly, and alone.
>
> **The per-trade price (CANON):** a market-relevant precognitive read costs **~0.1â€“0.5 Fathoms per trade** at small scale, rising steeply with position size and holding period (the deeper the read, the more of the pattern it rents). A desk running twenty reads a day burns ~2â€“10 Fathoms a *week* â€” a career measured in months. The expected lifetime P&L of a precog trader is negative once you price the selfhood. *"Lucky traders keep Drowning"* is not a proverb. It's a mortality table.
>
> **Crypto and offshore venues (CANON):** the compliance perimeter followed the money. Unregulated crypto venues are *not* outside the system: the Ledger's banking leverage (9.2 â€” soundings settle through member banks) means any venue that touches fiat on-ramps touches Lantern-screened compliance, and pure-crypto P&L still has to be *spent* somewhere. The "impossible luck" pattern-analysis runs on-chain too â€” Meridian Re's models don't care what the ledger is called. Two crypto-precog desks have Drowned since 2019; their wallets are case studies.

**Energy generation (free power).**
Fails on scale and visibility. Tide-tapped generation ([CORP-009](11_CORPORATIONS.md) Helios) works in pilot plants and nowhere else: output above trivial levels is Seismograph-visible, the Erosion cost of sustained channeling bankrupts the operator faster than the plant pays back, and Undertow-sourced energy has a documented habit of *doing something else* at the worst moment (Helios's 2020 "surplus event" in Nevada is the industry's cautionary tale). Verdict: a research subsidy, not a power grid.

**Suggestion-seeding markets (Choir manipulation).**
Fails on law and backlash. Direct mind control is impossible; suggestion seeding is resistible, produces backlash in the seeder (02, I), and Choir market manipulation carries the heaviest penalties in Accords law â€” the Tribunal treats it as an attack on the settlement system itself. Two convictions, 2002 and 2017; both defendants Drowned within eighteen months of sentencing, which the compliance manuals note without comment.

**Tide-mark viewing (seeing the past to trade on it).**
Fails on actionability. Tide-marks are viewable, never editable (02, I) â€” and viewing the past at *market-relevant* resolution requires Lantern work at T3+, which is Seismograph-visible, licensable, and auditable. Knowing what happened is not the same as being able to *prove* it to a counterparty, and the deepfake dividend (02, III) means nobody believes your Tide-mark readouts anyway. The information is real; the edge isn't.

**Information Seeps as insider trading.**
Fails on containment. Information Seeps (03, 3.3) are the rarest and hardest to contain â€” *you cannot put a fact in a vault*. Anyone who has traded on Seep-derived information has also *become* a vector for it. The Compact's information-hygiene doctrine treats this as a containment breach first and a crime second. There are no rich survivors of this trade. There are case files.

> CANON: The financial system survives contact with the supernatural for the same reason buildings survive earthquakes in Tokyo: it was designed by people who assumed the ground moves. Every control above exists because someone tried the exploit first.

## 9.7 The fiat firewall: the conversion protocol

> CANON: Soundings are quarantined inside the Ledger's closed system (9.2) â€” but Quiet *money* crosses into ordinary money every day: salaries, claim advances, materials sales. The crossing is legal, licensed, and the masquerade's load-bearing financial control.

**The protocol:**

1. **Licensed converters only.** The Ledger ([INTL-003](07_INTERNATIONAL_RELATIONS.md)) licenses seven member banks â€” [CORP-008](11_CORPORATIONS.md) Argent Vault chief among them â€” as the only legal Quietâ†”ordinary converters. Nobody else may convert at scale; the license is the bottleneck the whole system grips.
2. **Published rate.** Conversions price off the Ledger's quarterly SND reference band (9.2 â€” $12â€“16k in 2024) as negotiated FX-style deals. Large conversions move the band â€” and move it *visibly*, which is the point.
3. **Mandatory reporting.** Every conversion is reported to the Ledger. Conversions above threshold are additionally reported to the Seismograph Authority: a large conversion is a large operation's exhaust, and pattern-break analysis starts with the money.
4. **Licensed retail-edge crossings.** Ordinary payroll (salaries are ordinary money by design), [CORP-011](11_CORPORATIONS.md)'s rupiah bridge advances (9.1), and [CORP-003](11_CORPORATIONS.md) Blackforge's resonant-materials sales into ordinary supply chains (8.2.5) are *licensed* crossings, not violations â€” this is how Quiet money re-enters the ordinary economy without breaking the masquerade. Blackforge's Ravenhurst works operate under an SMD-licensed conversion path ([06_GOVERNMENTS.md](06_GOVERNMENTS.md) GOV-006).
5. **Unlicensed conversion is the crime.** Conversion outside the licensed path â€” the Gray Market's ([12_FACTIONS.md](12_FACTIONS.md) IND-006) founding business â€” is prosecuted as supernatural financial crime under the Accords' market-manipulation provisions (9.5). The firewall leaks at the retail edge by design; it breaks in the middle by prosecution.

**The seasoning rule (CANON).** Quiet-adjacent settlement of *physical* deliveries â€” bullion, materials, collateral â€” is value-dated **T+5**, outside the 72-hour borrowed-matter reversion window ([02_WORLD_RULES.md](02_WORLD_RULES.md) I). Delivery-versus-payment inside T+5 carries a mandatory **72-hour clawback**: if the delivered matter reverts, the trade unwinds automatically, and the reversion leaves a forensic Tide-mark (9.5 â€” the Zurich reversion's lesson, institutionalized). Borrowed gold cannot clear, because the settlement system now assumes it is borrowed until the window closes.

## REL-001 â€” The Order of the Veil (Vatican's anomaly office)

**Character:** cooperative, scholarly, old.

- **What it is:** a dicastery-level office of the Holy See (public-facing name unremarkable; internal name *Ordo Veli*), founded in its modern form in 1951, inheriting the four-century archive of its predecessor, the Veil Office ([24_HISTORY.md](24_HISTORY.md)). Roughly 400 staff worldwide: priests, nuns, lay scholars, and â€” quietly â€” a dozen Attuned professed in the Order's lay religious orders (brothers and sisters, never ordained: the 1378 prohibition on Attuned ordination, [24_HISTORY.md](24_HISTORY.md), is still enforced, and it is enforced *on* the dozen first).
- **Doctrine:** Seeps are *mysteria* â€” real, created-order phenomena that theology has not finished describing. The Order's founding principle, from its 1951 charter: *"We do not know what these things are; we know what they are not: they are not demons merely because they frighten us, and they are not miracles merely because we cannot explain them."* Attuned Catholics are understood as bearing a *charism* â€” morally neutral until used.
- **What it actually does:** archives (the Vatican's Seep archive is the oldest continuous phenomenological record on earth â€” some entries predate the Meridian Accords by 300 years), classification assistance to the Compact (the Order seconds scholars to [RES-001](15_EDUCATION.md) the Meridian Institute), and pastoral care: the Church runs the largest Quiet-care-adjacent counseling network in the world, most of whose counselors have no idea what they're actually treating.
- **Ordinary believers:** 1.4 billion Catholics, of whom ~1.399 billion know nothing. The Order's existence is need-to-know even inside the Curia. Parish priests encountering genuine Seeps are instructed (via a genuinely boring pastoral circular) to refer "persistent inexplicable phenomena" up the chain â€” which is how the Order finds most of its cases.
- **Relationship with the Compact:** the closest of any religion. The 1962 *Modus Vivendi* (secret) formalized cooperation: the Order shares archive access; the Compact shares redacted Seismograph data. Both sides have violated the spirit of it; neither has violated the letter.
- **Internal tension:** the scholars vs. the exorcists. The Office of Exorcism (a separate, older body) still operates on the demonic framework ([03_SUPERNATURAL_SYSTEM.md](03_SUPERNATURAL_SYSTEM.md) 3.2 â€” STATUS: IN-WORLD MISCONCEPTION, predictively useless), and the two offices have been in a cold bureaucratic war for seventy years. The scholars keep winning on results; the exorcists keep winning on parish popularity.

> STATUS: THEORY (the Order's own working position): Membrane Theory is compatible with Catholic metaphysics; the Tide's cause is "not a theological question until someone proves otherwise."

## REL-002 â€” The Marked Ministry (evangelical)

**Character:** earnest, fractured, loud in every sense.

- **What it is:** not one church but a movement: ~300 loosely affiliated evangelical and Pentecostal congregations (strongest in the US, Brazil, Nigeria, Indonesia, the Philippines) organized around a shared doctrine of the **Marked** â€” their term for the Attuned.
- **Doctrine:** the Marked bear a *sign*: some are blessed (healers, discerners â€” "gifts of the Spirit"), some are cursed (those whose channeling harms â€” "the enemy's counterfeit"). The split is the movement's central wound: the **Blessed wing** runs healing ministries and Attuned-integration programs; the **Counterfeit wing** preaches that most Attuned are demonized and campaigns for registration, restriction, and in the fringes, "deliverance by force."
- **Ordinary believers:** the vast majority are ordinary congregants who joined for the worship band and stayed for the community. Most have never met an Attuned and couldn't pick one out of a lineup. Their pastors' sermons about the Marked are, to them, sermons about *spiritual* gifts â€” the Veil Reflex ([03_SUPERNATURAL_SYSTEM.md](03_SUPERNATURAL_SYSTEM.md)) does the rest, quietly editing the one testimony that was real.
- **What it actually does:** the Blessed wing operates ~60 "discernment houses" â€” halfway houses for newly Awakened Attuned from evangelical backgrounds, teaching Erosion hygiene in the language of spiritual discipline. They are unlicensed, medically supervised by sympathetic doctors, and *statistically effective* â€” the Compact's medical directorate has the outcome data and doesn't know what to do with it.
- **Relationship with governments:** adversarial-to-wary. The Counterfeit wing lobbies hard for Choir-style restrictions on all Attuned; the Blessed wing lobbies for religious exemption from Census registration (lost in every jurisdiction so far). The movement is a permanent headache for threshold agencies â€” and, occasionally, their best source of voluntary Awakening reports.
- **Internal tension:** the Blessed/Counterfeit split is approaching schism. The 2022 "Tulsa statement" (Blessed wing affirming Attuned as "fearfully made") was denounced by Counterfeit leaders as heresy. Both sides claim the same scripture. Both sides are sincere.

> STATUS: IN-WORLD MISCONCEPTION (Counterfeit wing's core claim): Attuned channeling is demonic possession. Predictively useless, pastorally devastating, politically potent.

## The British religious field (no new IDs)

Albion's religious landscape matters because Ravenhurst â€” and much of the primary narrative ground â€” sits inside it.

- **Shinto shrine networks:** the country's oldest folk-containment layer. Small shrines mark Seeps the way buoys mark shoals: festivals, taboos, and *festival* calendars that route foot traffic around thin ground on the right days. Most *local clergy* are Loud and have no theory of the Tide; the practice works anyway. The SMD's field office keeps an unofficial map of shrine calendars and has stopped asking how the old priests know. (The shrines do not cooperate with the Compact, exactly. They were here first and behave accordingly.)
- **Buddhist temples:** the archival and pastoral layer. Old temples in KantÅ and Kansai hold parish-death registers that quietly double as Seep chronicles â€” a century of "drownings" nobody drowned in, annotated by abbots with excellent handwriting. Temple hospice networks do the same Quiet-care work as the Garden's hospices, in Buddhist idiom; several Garden houses in Albion rent rooms in temples. A few *sÅryo* lineages keep Erosion-hygiene manuals disguised as meditation manuals, which the scholars argue about at conferences.
- **New religions:** the mixed field. Postwar new-religion movements sit on top of the same ground â€” some run genuine support networks for the Awakened (quietly effective, pastorally sincere), some recruit Attuned aggressively as "proof" of doctrine (the SMD watches these), and a few are monitored because their leadership keeps asking very specific questions about tide tables. The Compact's standing position is that Albion's new religions are neither threat nor asset â€” they are *competition*, for the same hearts and the same ground.

- **Ideology:** *abundance*. Helios's founding faith: free energy ends every other problem, including the masquerade's. What's left of that faith is mostly in the marketing department.

- **Secrets:** (1) the 2020 Nevada "surplus event" produced 40 seconds of *structured* output â€” the tap didn't just surge, it *patterned*. Patel has a theory about what the pattern was. He has told no one, including Kim; (2) Patel's Erosion is accelerating faster than the models predict â€” the tap is *using him back*; (3) Halcyon's acquisition feelers have become pressure â€” a board member with defense ties has been pushing a sale, and Kim suspects she's being managed out.
- **Internal conflicts:** the believers (abundance is coming) vs. the engineers (the tap is a research instrument, not a power plant); Kim vs. the board; everyone vs. the question of what happens when Patel can't work anymore.

- **Allies:** The Quiet Garden (SUP-003) â€” uneasy mutual respect (both take Erosion seriously); the Ferrymen (SUP-010) â€” logistical cooperation; several REL actors (see `10_RELIGIONS.md`).
- **Secrets:** (1) The Tideguard maintains **"ark chapels"** â€” warded coastal vaults stocked for a post-masquerade world, including Drowndust counter-stockpiles "for defense." (2) Voice Prime Sarr privately doubts the Drowning-as-salvation doctrine's literal truth; her journals (seen by three people) frame it as "the kindest available lie." (3) The Choir's hospices are the hidden world's best **Erosion palliative-care network** â€” and therefore its best *recruitment pool for pre-Drowning Attuned with nothing left to lose*.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Reformists vs. Immersionists.** The reformist wing (young, urban, led by Jakarta's Tidewarden) wants the Choir to become a mainstream faith â€” interfaith dialogue, charity transparency, *renouncing* the ark chapels. The Immersionists want acceleration: deeper rituals, more Drownings-as-sacraments, open defiance of the Compact. The Cantorate balances on the split; Sarr's successor election (due within ~3 years) will decide it.
- **Public image:** Respected maritime charity with an eccentric theology. News profiles call them "the church of the drowned." Governments tolerate them because the hospices genuinely reduce public-health burdens.
- **Hidden agenda:** The ark chapels are not just defensive. Immersionist planners have war-gamed a **"guided Drowning"** scenario: if the masquerade collapses, the Choir intends to be the organization that *catches* the terrified Loud public â€” with doctrine, shelter, and a story that makes the horror meaningful. Whether that's salvation or the largest recruitment drive in history depends on who's telling it.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Venerates anomalies as "the Mother's handwriting." Maintains its own small catalog; has attempted contact with the eleven children of ANOMALY-015 four times. Refuses to approach ANOMALY-029 â€” the only thing the Choir fears, which terrifies everyone else.
- **Government relationship:** Licensed religious organization in 90+ countries. Watched (not harassed) by GOV-001, GOV-004, GOV-007. The Compact's official stance: "a faith, not a faction â€” until the Tideguard moves."

## SUP-002 â€” The Cartographers

**Type:** Independent research guild; the hidden world's mapmakers.

- **Origin:** 1921, from a split in a Royal Geographical Society expedition that found something in the Empty Quarter that wasn't on any map â€” because it moved. The survivors' rule: *map everything, sell to everyone, belong to no one*.
- **Leadership:** The **Atlas Table** â€” thirteen **Master Cartographers**, seats held by seniority of fieldwork, not politics. Current First of Table: **Master Ilya Petrov** (72, Hollow T2, 61 Fathoms â€” "retired from the field, not from arguing"). Decisions require nine of thirteen; the Table is famously slow and famously incorruptible, because every Master has survived enough thin places to be unimpressed by bribes.
- **Ideology:** Radical neutrality as methodology: a map that serves one faction is propaganda. Knowledge wants to be *priced*, not free â€” free maps get people killed by sending amateurs into T4 zones. Their creed: "We draw the shore. We don't tell you to swim."
- **Resources:** The **Atlas** â€” the most complete private survey of Place Seeps, thin places, Tide-pressure gradients, and Slipping recognition-points on earth. Subscription revenue from *everyone*: governments, corporations, cults, criminals. Field teams on every continent. Twelve of the thirteen Cartographer's Compasses (see ANOMALY-028); the thirteenth is Compact-borrowed.
- **Territory:** None claimed; **waystations** (neutral-ground hostels for field teams) in 40 cities â€” including Ravenhurst, the Pacific relay's new southern terminus â€” protected by universal custom â€” attacking a waystation gets you blacklisted from the Atlas, which every faction treats as a death sentence for logistics.
- **Members:** ~3,000 sworn Cartographers (field surveyors, archivists, instrumentsmiths); ~20,000 stringers and informants. Membership skews Lantern and Hollow Attuned; Loud civilians with good legs and better notebooks.
- **Recruitment:** Apprenticeship. Candidates are given a compass (ordinary), a notebook, and a one-way ticket to a T1 site. Half come back with a usable survey. The rest come back with a story, which the Cartographers also file.
- **Goals (stated):** Complete the Atlas; keep it neutral; keep surveyors alive.
- **Enemies:** The Ninth Bell (SUP-007) â€” the Bell murders Cartographers to keep thin places secret. Tide-noise jammers and map-forgers (several CRIM actors) who poison the data supply.
- **Allies:** Everyone, contractually; no one, actually. The Ferrymen (SUP-010) are their closest working partners (smugglers need maps; mapmakers need smugglers' routes).
- **Secrets:** (1) The Atlas has a **black layer** â€” surveys of sites too dangerous to sell, including three T6-adjacent locations. Four Masters know the full black layer exists. (2) The Cartographers have been *wrong* about the Tide's cause for a century and know it; their internal working paper ("we are mapping the *symptoms*") is the most honest document in the hidden world. (3) They maintain **dead-letter routes** â€” pre-arranged paths for moving people who need to disappear, used by defectors from every faction including, twice, the Compact itself. (4) **Ilsa Brandt's journals sat dormant-monitor for 28 years by protocol, not neglect:** the Exchange's standing rule is that the Laggard file activates only when a new holder surfaces â€” the inaction *was* the action, a tripwire left armed. Arthur Reed is the condition; Pram's 2024 find of the 1996 field map ([EVENT-100](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)) is the trigger; the reclassification of ANOMALY-001 from curiosity to priority is the tripwire firing.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Sellers vs. Sealers.** The commercial wing wants to monetize deeper layers (Pale Court money is *very* good). The Sealers â€” mostly old field hands â€” argue some maps should never be drawn, let alone sold. The black layer is the compromise; both sides think it's failing.
- **Public image:** They don't have one. The closest civilian equivalent is "that weird orienteering club with the good topographic maps." Their commercial map imprint (a hiking-map publisher) is genuinely excellent and profitable.
- **Hidden agenda:** The Cartographers are quietly building **evacuation cartography** â€” not for sale: routes, shelters, and recognition-points for a post-masquerade collapse, held in trust "for whoever needs them." The question the Table won't answer: who decides who needs them.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Professional and mercenary â€” anomalies are *terrain*. They broker first-survey rights the way mining firms broker claims.
- **Government relationship:** Licensed survey contractors to half the world's agencies; simultaneously the agencies' biggest intelligence headache, because the Cartographers sell the same map to the agency's enemies. Protected by the Meridian Accords' "neutral instruments" clause â€” a protection that is wearing thin as the High Tide raises the value of what they know.

## SUP-003 â€” The Quiet Garden

**Type:** Monastic order; the hidden world's Erosion hospice and stillness school.

- **Origin:** 1962, Kyoto â€” a Bone T4 (a trauma surgeon) who Drowned *slowly*, over eleven years, and spent the last three teaching other Attuned how to "sit still inside the pressure." Her students formalized the practice after her death. (Her name is recorded; the Garden does not speak it â€” "names are handles the Tide can grip.")
- **Leadership:** The **Still Abbots** â€” rotating council of seven, chosen by lot from members below 40 Fathoms (the Garden's one hard rule: no deeply Eroded person governs). Current convener: **Abbot Nguyen** (Vietnamese-French, 58, Lantern T3, 33 Fathoms).
- **Ideology:** Erosion is not a price to be paid but a *current to stop swimming against*. Through stillness disciplines (breath, attention, deliberate non-use), an Attuned can slow Erosion to a crawl and live a full life at low Fathoms. The Garden is pointedly *not* anti-power â€” it trains combat medics and crisis Lanterns â€” but it teaches that every channeling should be a conscious choice, never a reflex. (Their stillness techniques are the best-validated Erosion-slowing methods known; the Compact licenses the basic curriculum.)
- **Resources:** Modest but deep: **gardens** (monastery-sanatoria, always built on low-pressure ground) in 23 countries; the best Erosion-care clinicians alive; a library of first-person Drowning accounts (the "Falling Leaves archive") that every faction's doctors quietly consult. They take no fees â€” donations only â€” which makes them the only faction the poor trust unconditionally.
- **Territory:** The gardens themselves (Kyoto, Hue, Oaxaca, Fez, Ljubljana, Ravenhurst, and 17 others). The Jakarta garden is a converted colonial villa in Menteng with a waiting list of 400. The Ravenhurst garden â€” low-pressure "sitting lawns" on reclaimed waterfront ground, serving the port's Attuned â€” is the newest.
- **Members:** ~8,000 professed (monastics); ~60,000 lay affiliates. Attuned-heavy but deliberately mixed â€” the Garden insists the Loud and the Quiet belong in the same room, because "the Tide does not check your pattern before it takes you."
- **Recruitment:** Referral. Burned-out Attuned find the Garden the way alcoholics find meetings â€” someone who's been there tells them. The Garden also runs **open stillness classes** in 200 cities (marketed as meditation; it is, mostly).
- **Goals (stated):** Teach stillness; shelter the Eroding; record the Drowning honestly so the living can learn.
- **Enemies:** The Hollow Men (SUP-006) â€” the Garden considers Tide-junkie culture a desecration and Erosion trafficking an atrocity; the enmity is personal, not doctrinal, and it runs both ways. The Ninth Bell (SUP-007), which has bombed two gardens ("stillness is surrender" â€” the Bell's actual pamphlet line).
- **Allies:** The Drowned Choir (SUP-001) â€” mutual aid in hospice work; the Rememberers (IND-002); the Pro Bono Lanterns (IND-005), whom the Garden quietly trains.
- **Secrets:** (1) The Falling Leaves archive contains **three accounts of Drowning survived** â€” not reversed (impossible, 02.I), but *interrupted* at 99 Fathoms by means the Garden will not disclose and the Compact would classify as a weapon if it knew. (2) The Garden shelters **defectors** â€” Attuned fleeing every faction, including Compact black programs â€” under monastic sanctuary. The Compact knows and tolerates it, because the alternative is the defectors Drowning in public. (3) A small inner circle, the **Root**, believes stillness can do more than slow Erosion â€” that a sufficiently still mind can *become* a kind of living ward. They have been trying, quietly, for thirty years. Two Root members are currently... not Drowned, not alive, and the Garden's doctors use the word "seated."
- **Internal conflicts:** **Open vs. Closed.** The younger generation wants the Garden to go public â€” publish the stillness curriculum, lobby openly, become the hidden world's Red Cross. The elders argue visibility would destroy the thing that makes the Garden work: that nobody comes there to be *used*.
- **Public image:** A respected contemplative order with excellent palliative-care outcomes. Wellness magazines profile them; the profiles are always slightly wrong in ways the Garden finds restful.
- **Hidden agenda:** The Root's experiment. If a human mind can become a living ward â€” a person who *is* stillness, suppressing Tide pressure by existing â€” the Garden would hold the only countermeasure to the High Tide that isn't a weapon. They are also terrified of succeeding, because every faction would then want to *own* such a person.
- **Anomaly relationship:** The Garden keeps no anomalies and wants none. It does maintain the **"sitting list"** â€” places too sad or too pressured to leave unmarked, where a monastic sits in rotation, doing nothing, which somehow helps. ANOMALY-027's balcony is on the list.
- **Government relationship:** Beloved by health ministries, licensed by everyone, raided by no one. The Compact funds 30% of the Garden's clinical budget through cutouts and pretends it doesn't â€” because admitting the hidden world's best Erosion care is run by monks would embarrass the medical directorate.

## SUP-004 â€” The Red Ledger

**Type:** Private military company (public face) and gray-market brokerage (the Factor's black book); the hidden world's most professional mercenaries â€” and its most discreet auctioneers.

- **Origin:** 1977 â€” the Quiet Night. A Compact rapid-response company watched its government handlers order a Drowndust strike on a civilian district and *refused*. They walked off the contract, kept the name they'd given their unit's expense book ("the red ledger" â€” casualties were marked in red), and sold their services to whoever would sign their code.
- **Leadership:** The **Partners** â€” seven, currently led by **Partner Ayo Okafor** (Nigerian, 54, Tide T4, 58 Fathoms â€” "the most expensive soldier alive, and the one with the shortest clock, which she mentions in every negotiation"). Partnership is earned by ten years' service and a vote; Partners who hit 70 Fathoms retire to the Ledger's farm in Uruguay, no exceptions â€” the rule is named after the three who didn't.
- **Ideology:** **The Code.** (1) No Choir work (no crowd-scale emotional steering â€” "we're soldiers, not missionaries"). (2) No Drowndust, no infohazards, no children. (3) The contract is the contract â€” but a contract that requires breaking the Code is void, and the Ledger returns the fee *with interest* and blacklists the client. (4) Erosion accounting is honest: the Ledger quotes jobs in Fathoms as well as money, and refuses work it judges "not worth the depth." Clients mock this until they see the actuarial tables; the tables are always right. The Code is the PMC division's genuine operating ethic â€” and its public brand. The Partners' official position is that the Code binds the whole Ledger. The black book exists anyway (see Secrets), and the Partners' deniability is contractual, paper-thin, and priced into every black-book fee: the hypocrisy is the business model.
- **Resources:** ~2,400 personnel on the books (roughly 70% Attuned, T1â€“T4; the Ledger doesn't hire T5s â€” "we can't afford their funerals") â€” but only **a handful (under a dozen) hold combat licenses**, per Accords Art. VII. The rest are Loud logistics, medical, and legal staff, plus *non-combat-licensed* Attuned: field medics, Lantern examiners, Erosion counselors, Tide-noise technicians. The Ledger's muscle is reputation, retainers, and contracts â€” not battalions. Annual turnover ~$900M, mostly escrowed through Argent Vault (CORP-008).
- **Territory:** Headquartered in Montevideo (Uruguay's studied indifference is the point). Training grounds in the Sahel, the Carpathians, and (quietly) West Java. No territory claimed â€” the Ledger rents, everywhere.
- **Members:** Operators sign 5-year renewable contracts; support staff are mostly Loud civilians. Veterans' association is famously tight â€” the Ledger buries its own, and the funerals are the only events where rival factions' operators stand in the same room without weapons.
- **Recruitment:** Word of mouth and the **"red envelope"** â€” an unsolicited offer delivered to Attuned whose service records show Code-compatible ethics. Government special-operators approaching burnout are the prime pool; the Ledger's pitch is simple: "same work, honest accounting, no Drowndust."
- **Goals (stated):** Profit, professionalism, survival. The Ledger's Partners describe their strategic goal as "being the faction everyone hires and no one owns."
- **Enemies:** The Hollow Men (SUP-006) â€” the Ledger has a standing kill-on-sight policy for Erosion traffickers ("they sell our people's deaths back to them"); the Vostok Brotherhood (CRIM-004), a business rivalry that has turned bloody twice.
- **Allies:** Contractual only. Longest-standing client relationship: the Seismograph Authority (INTL-004) â€” disaster response retainers. The Cartographers (SUP-002) â€” mutual professional respect.
- **Secrets:** (1) The Ledger maintains a **"black book"** â€” not merely a list of clients who ordered Code-violating work, but an **active gray-market brokerage run by the Factor (CHAR-027)**: Rule auctions (the 2021 Trieste sale, [EVENT-084](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)), provenance escrow, and quiet inquiries for things that cannot legally be bought â€” including the 2024 Laggard inquiry ([EVENT-093](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)), which is trafficking under Accords law. The Factor's contracts are routed through three cutout layers; none are Ledger paper; the Partners do not acknowledge the brokerage, have never asked where its fees come from, and take their cut anyway. Three governments are in the book. (2) Partner Okafor is at 58 Fathoms and still taking field contracts; the Partners have voted twice to ground her and she's overruled them twice â€” the Code says nothing about Partners spending themselves, which everyone now agrees is an oversight. (3) The Ledger quietly *trains* Pro Bono Lanterns (IND-005) in field medicine, off the books.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Code vs. Market.** The High Tide has tripled demand and the Ledger is turning down 60% of contracts. A faction of younger Partners wants to loosen the Code (Choir work "for the right client," T5 hires) to meet demand. Okafor's position: "The Code is the product. Without it we're just the Hollow Men with better uniforms."
- **Public image:** Doesn't exist publicly. In the hidden world: the gold standard â€” expensive, honest, and the only mercenaries whose contracts hold up in Tribunal arbitration.
- **Hidden agenda:** The Partners are building a **post-Compact contingency**: escrowed funds, cached warded facilities, and pre-negotiated contracts with Gray Market authorities, so that if the masquerade collapses, the Ledger becomes the security backbone of whatever comes next â€” *before* anyone else can. They call it "the pension plan."
- **Anomaly relationship:** Strictly professional â€” anomalies are *objectives*, handled per contract. The Ledger's PMC division refuses anomaly-trafficking contracts (Code: "we're not couriers for things that eat couriers"). The Factor's black book brokers them anyway â€” including inquiries into person-attached tethers, which the law treats as trafficking ([14_LAW_ENFORCEMENT.md](14_LAW_ENFORCEMENT.md) 14.3(2)).
- **Government relationship:** Licensed PMC in 40+ jurisdictions; on retainer to INTL-004 and three GOV agencies. The Compact's Joint Containment Command (INTL-006) uses the Ledger as its deniable surge capacity â€” an arrangement both sides describe as "regrettable and necessary."

## SUP-005 â€” The Lantern Bearers

**Type:** Vigilante anomaly-hunter network; the hidden world's most divisive volunteers.

- **Origin:** 2001, from a Usenet group ("alt.paranormal.response") whose members â€” mostly Loud civilians and low-tier Attuned â€” started *showing up* at Seep sites with cameras, first-aid kits, and more courage than training. When a Bearers cell contained a T3 Place Seep in Ohio before the Compact arrived, the network went from hobby to institution.
- **Leadership:** There isn't any, formally. The network runs on **"lantern protocol"** â€” open-source field manuals, regional signal-chat coordination, and reputation. The closest thing to leaders are the **Keepers**, a dozen veteran organizers (rotating, recallable) who maintain the manuals and the bail fund. Current most-prominent Keeper: **Mara Iversen** (Norwegian, 44, Lantern T2, Loud-born civilian journalist).
- **Ideology:** "Someone has to go." The Bearers believe the Compact is too slow, too secretive, and too willing to write off civilians â€” so ordinary people should be *equipped*, not just protected. Their manuals teach Rule-observation, Tide-noise basics, and above all: *call the Compact, but don't wait for them*.
- **Resources:** Crowdfunded (~$40M/year in donations, mostly small), plus the **bail fund** and a volunteer legal network. Equipment is improvised â€” the Bearers' famous "lantern kits" (Tide-pressure strips, Stillwater injectors, warded tarps) are assembled in garages. What they lack in funding they make up in *numbers and proximity*: a Bearer is usually already on the scene.
- **Territory:** Everywhere with internet. Strongest in North America, Brazil, Nigeria, and â€” increasingly â€” Southeast Asia, where the Jakarta cell ("Obor") is 400 strong and uncomfortably competent â€” and now East Asia, where a Ravenhurst cell (**"Akari"** â€” British for "light") is coalescing around NQA's night-shift clerks.
- **Members:** ~60,000 claimed affiliates; ~8,000 active field volunteers. Mostly Loud civilians and T1â€“T2 Attuned. Median age 26. Turnover is brutal â€” the average field career lasts 18 months before burnout, injury, or a quiet word from a government.
- **Recruitment:** The manuals are public. Anyone can declare themselves a Bearer; the network's only gatekeeping is the Keepers' quiet practice of *talking the reckless ones out of it* â€” which works about half the time.
- **Goals (stated):** Protect civilians from Seeps; document honestly; force the Compact to be faster and more transparent.
- **Enemies:** The Ninth Bell (SUP-007) â€” Bearers have died stopping Bell operations, and the Bell returns the favor. The Hollow Men (SUP-006), who prey on the same vulnerable civilians. Various governments that prosecute them for "interfering with containment."
- **Allies:** The Static Hour (IND-001) â€” mutual amplification; the Rememberers (IND-002) â€” shared membership; the Pro Bono Lanterns (IND-005) â€” field cooperation. Sympathetic elements inside GOV agencies (especially junior BPF officers in Jakarta) leak them warnings.
- **Secrets:** (1) The Keepers maintain a **quiet list** of ~200 Bearers who've gone too far â€” "liabilities": glory-seekers, livestreamers, two confirmed Bell infiltrators â€” and the network *steers work away from them* without ever formally expelling anyone. (2) The bail fund is partly financed by **Pale Court money** (SUP-009) â€” old families who find vigilantes *useful* and deniable. The Keepers hate this and can't afford to refuse it. (3) Three Bearer cells have standing **"do not call the Compact"** policies for certain Seep types â€” they're running their own containment experiments, unlicensed, uninsured.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Heroes vs. Liabilities.** The network's founding ethos (anyone can help) collides with its casualty rate. The Keepers' reform wing wants licensing, training standards, and Compact integration; the old guard calls that "becoming the thing we started to shame." The Jakarta Obor cell is the flashpoint â€” it's professionalizing fast, and nobody's sure whether that's salvation or capture.
- **Public image:** Among civilians who've heard of them: folk heroes ("the people who showed up"). Among governments: a nuisance at best, a danger at worst. Among the Compact: "courageous, untrained, and statistically doomed â€” but they *were* first on the scene in Lagos, so we take their calls."
- **Hidden agenda:** The Keepers' long game is **legitimacy**: they want the Meridian Accords' next revision to recognize civilian first-response â€” a legal status, funding, training. Every manual update, every documented save, is evidence for a negotiation most Bearers don't know is happening.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Hands-on and reverent â€” Bearers *name* the Seeps they work (their field names often stick; ANOMALY-024's "Umbrella Crow" is a Bearers coinage). They oppose anomaly trafficking on principle and have raided two Ash Exchange (CRIM-003) auctions.
- **Government relationship:** Legally gray everywhere; explicitly illegal in China, Russia, and Iran; tacitly tolerated in Indonesia, Brazil, and Nigeria â€” where agencies quietly use them as tripwires. GOV-004 (BPF) has an unofficial "don't arrest the Obor unless they're filming" policy. The SMD's Ravenhurst desk has the new Akari cell under quiet observation â€” too early for a policy; a foreign-worker night-shift cell is an immigration file as much as a supernatural one.

## SUP-006 â€” The Hollow Men

**Type:** Tide-junkie subculture and Erosion-trafficking network; the hidden world's open wound.

- **Origin:** No founding, only accretion â€” since the 1970s, Attuned chasing the *feeling* of channeling (the "tide-rush," a documented neurochemical event) found each other in squats, clubs, and veterans' wards. The trafficking layer â€” selling Erosion *itself* â€” emerged in the 1990s when someone realized a pre-Drowning Attuned's final channeling could be *directed*.
- **Leadership:** None that admits it. The scene runs on **"conductors"** â€” organizers who arrange sessions, source Stillwater, and take cuts. The trafficking tier is run by perhaps a dozen **"fences"** (the Compact has names for four). The most notorious: **"Mother's Milk"**, a fence believed to operate out of the Sahel Gray Markets, who brokers "last dives" â€” commissions where a dying Attuned spends their final Fathoms on a buyer's target.
- **Ideology:** To the extent it has one: *the Tide is the only honest thing*. Pain, Erosion, Drowning â€” at least they're real, unlike the Compact's paperwork and the Garden's sermons. Most Hollow Men aren't ideologues; they're addicts, burnouts, and deserters self-medicating with pressure.
- **Resources:** Cash-heavy, asset-light. Revenue from tide dens (entry fees, Stillwater sales), Erosion trafficking ("last dives" start at $2M), and *grief tourism* â€” wealthy clients paying to "feel something real." No territory held; dens migrate.
- **Territory:** Wherever the desperate gather â€” port districts, post-industrial zones, festival circuits. Notable dens: the **Sunken Chapel** (Naples), **Kilometer 12** (outside Nairobi), the **Milk Bar** (a moving venue, currently rumored in Surabaya).
- **Members:** ~15,000 scene participants; ~2,000 hardcore; the trafficking tier maybe 300. Mostly Attuned T1â€“T3 in the 40â€“80 Fathom band â€” people with power, damage, and nothing left to lose.
- **Recruitment:** Gravity. Burned-out operators, discharged soldiers, failed Garden cases â€” the scene absorbs everyone the hidden world's institutions drop. The fences recruit "last divers" from hospices, which is why the Drowned Choir (SUP-001) wants them dead.
- **Goals (stated):** None, collectively. Individually: the next rush, the next session, one more dive.
- **Enemies:** Everyone with a Code. The Red Ledger (SUP-004) hunts their fences; the Quiet Garden (SUP-003) considers them a desecration; the Lantern Bearers (SUP-005) raid their dens; the Drowned Choir (SUP-001) wants "last dive" brokers excommunicated from humanity. Even the Ninth Bell finds them distasteful ("hedonists, not faithful").
- **Allies:** The Ash Exchange (CRIM-003) â€” business partners in Drowning-site exploitation. Corrupt elements in various agencies who buy "last dives" off the books.
- **Secrets:** (1) The "last dive" market's biggest buyers are **not** criminals â€” they're *governments and corporations*, purchasing deniable T4â€“T5 effects with no Erosion on their own books. The fences keep receipts. (2) "Mother's Milk" is believed to be a **former Compact medical directorate officer** â€” which is why the Compact's Hollow Men task force keeps getting stood down. (3) The scene's tide dens are, inadvertently, the hidden world's most effective **early-warning network** for pressure spikes â€” junkies feel the Tide rise before the Seismograph does. Three agencies quietly monitor den chatter.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Users vs. Used.** The scene romanticizes itself as a community of the honest damned; the trafficking tier treats the community as *inventory*. "Last divers" are celebrated in den mythology and mourned by no one with power â€” the contradiction is the scene's open secret.
- **Public image:** Invisible to the public; in the hidden world, spoken of the way sailors speak of reefs â€” with contempt and navigational respect.
- **Hidden agenda:** The fences' endgame is **leverage**: receipts for every "last dive" ever brokered, held against the day the buyers' governments need to be reminded who really ordered what. It's a dead-man's archive aimed at the powerful.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Parasitic â€” dens often form *around* Place Seeps (free pressure), and fences have sold "guided sessions" inside uncontained sites. They've also, twice, *created* anomalies: both times a "last dive" ended in Drowning, exactly as the Rulebooks say it would.
- **Government relationship:** Hunted everywhere, protected nowhere â€” officially. Unofficially, at least four intelligence services maintain "don't touch" lists covering specific fences, because the receipts cut both ways.

## SUP-007 â€” The Ninth Bell

**Type:** Apocalyptic cult; the hidden world's most wanted true believers. **Threat level (both):** the Bell's *cells* (3â€“8 operatives) are a **tactical** threat â€” sabotage, thinning, murder; the **Peal** (the nine-site eschaton) is a **strategic** threat â€” a planned Threshold event the JCC spends more on than any other non-state actor. Doctrine files both: the cells get noise-farmed containment, the Peal gets the full anomaly-war ladder (13_MILITARY.md 13.7).

- **Origin:** 1988, from a schism in a Drowned Choir chapter in Antwerp. The schismatics' doctrine: the Mother Below isn't *waking* â€” she's *knocking*, and the Membrane is the door. Their name comes from their founding ritual: eight bells for the eight founders, and a ninth, unrung, "for the hour of the opening."
- **Leadership:** The **Peal** â€” a council of **eight Rectors**, identities unknown (the Compact has confirmed two, suspects four). Below them, **cells** of 3â€“8, organized on classic clandestine lines. Defectors describe leadership not as charismatic but as *certain* â€” "they don't persuade you, they *inform* you, the way a doctor informs you."
- **Ideology:** The Membrane is a *wound that learned to call itself skin*. The Tide isn't salvation (the Choir's error) â€” it's *pressure against a door that should never have been closed*. The Bell's project: **thin the Membrane deliberately** â€” sabotage wards, crack containment, seed pressure spikes â€” until the door opens and humanity "remembers what it was before it agreed to be small." Mass Drowning isn't a cost to them; it's *the congregation arriving all at once*. (STATUS: THEORY â€” theology. Every other faction's assessment, including the Choir's: "they've mistaken the ocean for a mother and drowning for baptism.")
- **Resources:** Lean and fanatical. Funding from true-believer tithing, a handful of sympathetic Pale Court (SUP-009) eccentrics, and *theft* â€” the Bell robs Gray Market shipments the way other cults pass collection plates. Their real resource is **willingness**: Bell operatives accept Drowning as a mission outcome, which makes them the only faction that can spend lives the way others spend money.
- **Territory:** None. Cells in 30+ countries; heaviest in the Low Countries, the Balkans, and (recently) Java â€” the Jakarta cell is BPF's most-wanted, and the new Ravenhurst cells are the SMD's newest watch-list.
- **Members:** ~5,000 adherents; ~400 operatives. Recruitment skews young, brilliant, and *grieving* â€” the Bell recruits where the Choir recruits, which is why the two are at theological war.
- **Recruitment:** "The Question." Bell recruiters don't pitch; they ask one question â€” usually about a personal loss â€” and listen. The doctrine does the rest. Counter-cult specialists call it the most effective radicalization funnel in the hidden world, because it *starts* with genuine pastoral care.
- **Goals (stated):** Thin the Membrane; ring the Ninth Bell (their eschaton â€” a coordinated multi-site pressure event they've been planning for decades); "wake the dreamers."
- **Enemies:** Everyone. Formally at war with the Compact (INTL-001), the Drowned Choir (SUP-001, theological hatred), and the Cartographers (SUP-002, whose people they murder). The Red Ledger (SUP-004) has a standing contract â€” client confidential, widely guessed â€” for Bell Rectors, dead or (preferably) talkative.
- **Allies:** None, by doctrine ("allies are hostages you haven't taken yet"). Temporary convergences with the Hollow Men (SUP-006) for logistics and the Ash Exchange (CRIM-003) for Drowndust â€” both of which the Bell regards with open contempt.
- **Secrets:** (1) The Bell's eschaton plan â€” **"the Peal"** â€” targets *nine* sites simultaneously, including ZONE-007's perimeter (ANOMALY-029). The Compact knows eight of the nine. The ninth is the subject of the largest quiet manhunt in the hidden world. (2) Two of the eight Rectors are **former Compact personnel** â€” one a Seismograph analyst, one a containment architect. They know exactly how the defenses work, because they built them. (3) The Bell has been *right* about one thing: their 2017 pamphlet predicted the Seismograph baseline drift three years before the Authority published it. Nobody in power will say this aloud.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Peal vs. Parish.** The operatives want the eschaton *now*; the Rectors keep delaying ("the ninth bell is not rung early"). A younger faction, the **Tenth Bell** heresy, argues the Rectors have gone soft and the thinning should be *continuous and public*. The Rectors have excommunicated (read: killed) three Tenth Bell organizers. The heresy persists.
- **Public image:** None â€” they're ghosts. When they surface (the 2017 Istanbul attempt, the 2021 Trieste bombing), coverage treats them as terrorists, which is accurate and incomplete.
- **Hidden agenda:** The Peal. Everything â€” the cells, the thefts, the murders of Cartographers â€” is preparation for nine simultaneous thinnings. What the rank and file don't know: the Rectors' models show the Peal killing *millions*, and the Rectors consider that "the first honest number anyone's used."
- **Anomaly relationship:** Instrumental and blasphemous (even the Choir says so): anomalies are *tools for thinning* â€” Drowndust feedstock, pressure-spike triggers, weapons. They attempted to weaponize ANOMALY-020 (the Bell That Rings Backwards) in 2017; BPF's file on the attempt is 900 pages.
- **Government relationship:** Designated terrorist organization in 60+ countries. Every GOV agency has a Bell desk. The Compact's Joint Containment Command (INTL-006) spends more on the Bell than on any other non-state actor â€” and is *losing*, slowly, because you can't deter people who've already accepted Drowning.

## SUP-008 â€” The Archivists of the Second Silence

**Type:** Secret historical order; keepers of the pre-1949 hidden history.

- **Origin:** Older than the Compact. The Archivists trace themselves to a 17th-century Venetian *scriptorium* that copied "books that burned readers" â€” and learned, by trial and fatal error, how to handle informational Seeps. They were the hidden world's memory *before* the Meridian Accords, and they've never forgiven the Accords for making memory a state function.
- **Leadership:** The **Readers** â€” a council of senior archivists, currently convened by **Reader Emeritus Yusuf Adeyemi** (Nigerian-British, 77, un-Attuned, Loud â€” "the most dangerous librarian alive," per a Compact director who meant it fondly). Leadership is by *tenure of reading*: you advance by having read more of the Archive (ANOMALY-030) than anyone else and survived with judgment intact.
- **Ideology:** **The past is a person.** Not metaphor â€” doctrine. History isn't data; it's a *survivor*, and survivors deserve the courtesy of being heard on their own terms, not mined for lessons. Hence the Archive's Rule (read, don't extract; visit, don't index) isn't just containment â€” it's *manners*. The Archivists oppose the Compact's classification regime on philosophical grounds: "You file the dead. We *host* them."
- **Resources:** The **Second Silence Archive** (ANOMALY-030) â€” the largest pre-1949 collection in existence, and self-protecting. Plus scriptoria (fortified libraries) in Venice, Timbuktu, Yogyakarta, and Oaxaca; a bindery that produces the only reliably rot-resistant paper known (the recipe is itself an informational Seep, and the Archivists will not discuss it); and the finest provenance-researchers alive.
- **Territory:** The scriptoria, plus the **Yogyakarta scriptorium** â€” Southeast Asia's anchor, housed in a former sultanate library, staffed partly by *abdi dalem* families who've served it for six generations.
- **Members:** ~1,200 sworn Archivists; ~5,000 "borrowers" (cleared readers). Skewed old, Loud, multilingual, and stubborn. The order's median age is 58; its youngest Reader is 49. They are *all* like this.
- **Recruitment:** Bequest. Archivists recruit from historians, rare-book dealers, and â€” their favorite pool â€” **retired intelligence analysts** with clearances, regrets, and time. Initiation involves reading one document from the Archive's outer layer and writing about it honestly; the Archive itself judges the initiate (two candidates have been... declined, and will not speak of it).
- **Goals (stated):** Preserve; curate; *witness*. The Archivists' strategic goal is that no faction â€” especially not the Compact â€” ever holds a monopoly on the past.
- **Enemies:** The Ninth Bell (SUP-007), which wants to burn the Archive ("the past is an anchor"); information-brokers who steal and sell documents (several CRIM actors); and, institutionally, the Compact's classification directorate â€” a cold war fought in footnotes.
- **Allies:** The Cartographers (SUP-002) â€” fellow neutrals, mutual exchange (maps for histories); the Quiet Garden (SUP-003) â€” shared reverence; university history departments (unwitting, mostly).
- **Secrets:** (1) The Archivists hold **the 1949 file** â€” the complete, unredacted negotiating record of the Meridian Accords, including the names of the three signatories who were *already Drowned* and nobody noticed. This is their ultimate leverage; they've never used it. (2) The Yogyakarta scriptorium holds **Arthur-adjacent material** â€” pre-war Batavia insurance records showing Quiet Insurance's *original* purpose, which was not insurance. (Drafter D's territory; noted here as a loaded gun.) (3) The Archive is *growing* â€” new documents surface in it that no Archivist accessioned, all pre-1949 in content, all in hands that match no known scribe. The Readers call these "the deposits." They have stopped logging them where the Compact can see.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Openers vs. Keepers.** The Openers (younger, many ex-journalists) want to *publish* â€” carefully, slowly, starting with the least dangerous layers â€” arguing the masquerade's decay makes secrecy obsolete. The Keepers argue the Archive's self-protection proves the dead *don't want* publishing, and that the Openers are confusing their own curiosity with the dead's consent. The debate has run for forty years; the High Tide is tipping it toward the Openers.
- **Public image:** None publicly. Academically: "that eccentric private library in Venice with the impossible catalogue." In the hidden world: the conscience nobody invited but everybody consults.
- **Hidden agenda:** The Archivists are preparing a **"reading"** â€” a controlled, supervised disclosure of selected pre-1949 history to the Compact's leadership, timed for the moment the masquerade can no longer hold. Their goal: ensure the post-secrecy world inherits *context*, not just panic. They've been preparing it for twenty years. It's almost ready. Almost.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Curatorial â€” the Archive (ANOMALY-030) *is* their anomaly, and their whole institutional design is a centuries-long negotiation with it. They also authenticate anomalies' histories for a fee (the Pale Court's provenance certificates all pass through Venice).
- **Government relationship:** Princely. The Archivists predate every modern agency and behave like it â€” they receive ambassadors, not inspectors. The Compact's official arrangement (reading privileges, no copies) is the envy of every intelligence service; three have tried to replicate it by theft, and the Archive's immune response (see ANOMALY-030) handled all three.

## SUP-009 â€” The Pale Court

**Type:** Old-money dynastic network; collectors of anomalies as status, power, and hobby.

- **Origin:** No founding date â€” the Court *accreted* from European, Ottoman, Mughal, and Qing-era families who were already collecting "curiosities" when curiosities started being *anomalous*. The name comes from a 19th-century Viennese salon joke: "the court with no king, only paleness" (they've always been proud of being bloodless about it).
- **Leadership:** The **Table** â€” not a council but a *social fact*: roughly forty family heads whose consensus is tracked the way meteorologists track pressure. Current first-among-equals: **Contessa Elena Vidal** (Spanish-Italian, 68, un-Attuned, Loud â€” "the woman who has owned three governments' debts and never raised her voice"). Decisions happen at **the Season** â€” annual gatherings (Venice, Kyoto, Marrakech) that are equal parts auction, marriage market, and summit.
- **Ideology:** **Custodianship as superiority.** The Court's sincere belief: anomalies are *wasted* on governments (which weaponize them) and cults (which worship them); they belong with people of *taste, patience, and long horizons* â€” i.e., families that measure time in centuries. This is aristocratic self-flattery, but it produces genuinely excellent conservation: Court-held anomalies are the best-maintained in the world.
- **Resources:** Absurd. Combined family wealth in the low trillions; private warded vaults on five continents; the finest provenance-forgers and art lawyers money can buy (which is how Court pieces stay "private collections" through every Compact audit); and **dynastic Attuned** â€” the Court's breeding programs are the closest thing to reliable Awakening pipelines in existence (still unreliable â€” 04_POWER_SYSTEM.md Â§4.1 holds â€” but the Court's children Awaken at 30Ã— baseline, and the Court *notices* which marriages produce it).
- **Territory:** Estates, not territory â€” palazzi, compounds, islands. Notable: the **Vidal palazzo** (Venice), the **Blackforge-adjacent** holdings (see CORP-003 â€” the Blackforge family straddles Court and corporate worlds), and the **Surabaya freeport vaults** (the Court's Southeast Asian anchor, run by the Tanuwijaya family).
- **Members:** ~40 core families (~4,000 individuals); ~15,000 retainers, curators, and "friends of the family." Attuned members are prized and *managed* â€” the Court treats its Attuned the way it treats its art: insured, displayed, never risked.
- **Recruitment:** Birth and marriage. The Court *adopts* selectively â€” brilliant Loud outsiders (curators, Lanterns, the occasional Night Clerk who notices too much) are offered patronage that is very hard to refuse. The Ravenhurst branch's records clerk â€” perfect recall, no power, no protectors â€” would interest them enormously; the Court has a file on "promising clerks" the way universities have scouting lists.
- **Goals (stated):** Preserve, collect, appreciate. The Court's strategic goal: ensure that whatever comes after the masquerade, the *best pieces* â€” and the families that hold them â€” survive the transition with their positions intact.
- **Enemies:** Thieves (especially the Ash Exchange, CRIM-003, which has robbed three Court vaults); the Ninth Bell (SUP-007) â€” the Bell considers collectors "hoarders of the sacred" and has targeted two Seasons; tax authorities (the eternal enemy).
- **Allies:** The Cartographers (SUP-002) â€” best customers; the Archivists (SUP-008) â€” provenance; the Ferrymen (SUP-010) â€” logistics, discreetly. Sympathetic legislators everywhere (the Court *is* the donor class).
- **Secrets:** (1) The Court's vaults hold **four unregistered T4+ anomalies** â€” pieces the Compact doesn't know exist, including one the Contessa privately calls "the succession piece." (2) The dynastic breeding programs have produced **two T5 Attuned** in three generations; both were steered into quiet lives (one is a Kyoto gardener; the Compact has no idea). (3) The Court maintains a **"poor book"** â€” blackmail-grade material on every politician, regulator, and Compact official their families have entertained for a century. It's never been used. That's why it works.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Collectors vs. Players.** The traditionalists want the Court to remain above politics â€” collect, preserve, endure. The Players (younger heads, led by a Tanuwijaya scion) want to *use* the collection: anomaly-backed finance, political leverage, a seat at the Compact's table rather than the children's table. The Season's debates are civilized and vicious.
- **Public image:** Philanthropists, patrons of the arts, names on museum wings. The art world knows them; the hidden world knows what the art *is*.
- **Hidden agenda:** **The succession piece.** The Contessa is 68 and the Players are restless; the unregistered T4+ in the Venice vault is reportedly intended as the instrument of a managed transition â€” though whether it secures the Court's future or the Contessa's is the question nobody asks aloud.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Proprietary and loving â€” the Court *collects*, which means it also *protects*. Court-held anomalies have the lowest incident rates in the world. The Compact's unofficial position: "we disapprove of everything about them except their safety record, which is better than ours."
- **Government relationship:** Deeply entwined â€” the Court doesn't lobby governments so much as *staff* them (second cousins in ministries on four continents). The Compact's oversight of Court holdings is real but gentle; the poor book ensures it stays that way.

## SUP-010 â€” The Ferrymen

**Type:** Smugglers' confederation; movers of people and anomalies across borders.

- **Origin:** 1950s, Trieste â€” dockworkers and fishermen who'd always moved *things* past customs realized the new hidden world needed moving *differently*. The founding compact (the "First Toll," see ANOMALY-022) was simple: *we carry anything except Drowndust and infohazards, we ask no questions, we never talk about cargo*.
- **Leadership:** The **Harbor Council** â€” nine route-bosses ("Harbor Masters"), currently chaired by **"Old Marta"** (Triestine, 71, un-Attuned, Loud â€” a legend who has personally carried three defectors, two T3 anomalies, and one pregnant woman across four borders in a single week in 1996 and will tell you about it if you buy the wine). Authority is by route-control, not rank; Council decisions are enforced by the oldest sanction in smuggling: *no one will carry for you again*.
- **Ideology:** **The border is the fiction; the crossing is the truth.** The Ferrymen are philosophically opposed to containment-by-geography â€” if the Compact wants something kept in one country, that's the Compact's problem, not the Ferrymen's. Their code (the only morality they claim): no Drowndust, no infohazards, no children moved against their will, and *never* give up a passenger. They've kept the code for seventy years, which is why even the Compact uses them.
- **Resources:** Routes, not assets: the **Salt Road** corridors (see CRIM-005 â€” the Ferrymen *use* the Salt Road; they don't own it, a distinction both sides enforce carefully), Adriatic fast boats, Sahel overland chains, Pacific fishing-fleet relays â€” including the growing **Vladivostokâ€“Ravenhurst Pacific relay** (the primary region's northern door) and its Ravenhurst dead drops â€” and the **Punctual Fog** (ANOMALY-014) dead-drop window in Trieste. Plus the Lantern of the First Toll (ANOMALY-022) â€” their founding relic and moral compass, literally.
- **Territory:** None held; *everywhere crossed*. Waystations in 60+ port and border cities, often shared (unknowingly) with Cartographers' waystations â€” the two networks' overlap is the hidden world's worst-kept secret.
- **Members:** ~6,000 sworn Ferrymen (boat crews, drivers, guides, "aunts" â€” the safe-house keepers); ~30,000 occasional contractors. Notably *un*-Attuned-heavy â€” the Ferrymen prefer mundanes, because Attuned draw Seismograph attention and "a boat is quieter than a miracle."
- **Recruitment:** Vouching. Two sworn Ferrymen vouch, you carry three probationary runs, the Harbor Council votes. Washout rate is low; betrayal rate is lower â€” the sanction (no one carries for you, ever, and everyone *knows*) is social death in the only community most Ferrymen have.
- **Recruitment note:** They recruit *defectors* constantly â€” not as members but as cargo. The Ferrymen have moved Attuned out of every faction's reach, including (twice) the Compact's own black programs. Their passenger manifest is the hidden world's most dangerous document; it doesn't exist on paper.
- **Goals (stated):** Keep the routes open; keep the code. The Ferrymen's strategic goal is *permanence*: to be the infrastructure nobody can afford to destroy.
- **Enemies:** Border agencies (professional rivalry, not hatred); the Ash Exchange (CRIM-003) â€” the Exchange poaches Ferrymen routes for Drowndust, violating the code's spirit; the Ninth Bell (SUP-007), which has murdered Ferrymen who refused Bell cargo.
- **Allies:** The Cartographers (SUP-002) â€” maps for routes, the oldest partnership in the hidden world; the Drowned Choir (SUP-001) â€” maritime cooperation; the Night Clerks (IND-004) â€” information symbiosis in port cities.
- **Secrets:** (1) The Ferrymen maintain **"the Quiet Ledger"** â€” not cargo records (those don't exist) but *debt* records: who owes whom for what crossing. Three governments, two corporations, and one Compact directorate are in it. (2) Old Marta's 1996 run included a passenger the Council voted to forget â€” a child, moved *toward* danger, not away. The code was bent once. The Council still isn't sure it was wrong. (3) The Ferrymen have a standing arrangement with the Memorandum Group (INTL-007): certain "diplomatic pouches" travel Ferrymen routes with full code protection â€” which means the world's spies trust smugglers more than they trust each other.
- **Internal conflicts:** **Code vs. Hunger.** The High Tide has made smuggling *immensely* profitable â€” and immensely dangerous. Younger crews want to take Drowndust contracts ("the code was written when Drowndust was rare; it's currency now"). The Council's position, enforced twice by sanction: the code is the business. Without it, they're just criminals with boats.
- **Public image:** None â€” they're ghosts with good boats. Port police worldwide know *of* them the way they know of weather.
- **Hidden agenda:** The Ferrymen are building **"the Last Route"** â€” a fully mapped, fully crewed evacuation corridor from every major hidden-world population center to Gray Market sanctuaries, for the day the masquerade fails. It's the largest humanitarian logistics project nobody's ever heard of, and it's 70% complete.
- **Anomaly relationship:** Professional carriers â€” anomalies are cargo, handled per the code. They've carried everything except the two forbidden classes, and their safety record (zero *reported* lost cargoes in seventy years â€” the record is *reported* perfect: the Compact's loss-database disagrees in three cases the Ferrymen classify as "delivered to an alternate consignee," and everyone involved understands what that euphemism costs) is why the Compact *lets* them operate.
- **Government relationship:** The open secret: every intelligence service uses Ferrymen routes and pretends not to know them. GOV-004 (BPF) has an unacknowledged "harbor understanding" with the Jakarta crews â€” BPF doesn't inspect certain boats; the Ferrymen don't carry Bell cargo through Indonesian waters. Both sides keep the fiction because the alternative is war on the docks.
