# 30 â€” POWER HIERARCHY: T0â€“T7 in Practical Terms

> CANON: Tier measures **maximum sustainable output** â€” nothing else. Not skill, not danger, not Erosion rate, not intelligence, not preparation. This file is the practical manual: what each tier can and cannot do, what power *costs* at each tier, and â€” the load-bearing section â€” **how the weak survive the strong**, because the entire novel runs on that mechanic. System foundations in [04_POWER_SYSTEM.md](04_POWER_SYSTEM.md).

## 30.1 The tiers, practically

| Tier | Name | Can (sustained) | Cannot | The one-line truth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T0 | Quiet | Everything ordinary humans can do â€” including killing an Attuned with a rifle | Channel deliberately | The tier that wins wars: 8 billion people, logistics, law |
| T1 | Spark | Party tricks; light a cigarette with a thought; sense pressure; minor mending | Anything decisive; anything unnoticed at scale | Inconvenient or charming; the hidden world's plankton |
| T2 | Lantern | Professional-grade work: read a room's Tide-marks, shatter a door, heal a fracture, calm a crowd, wade briefly | Decide a battle; act at distance; sustain output for hours | The working class of the hidden world â€” 90,000 professionals |
| T3 | Surge | Decide a firefight or a boardroom; breach wards; slip across a city; steer a room's emotions | Act without being Seismograph-visible; fight an army; hide the cost | Registered, watched, licensed â€” power with paperwork |
| T4 | Tempest | National-asset effects: weather-working a county, leveling a building, crowd-scale suggestion, intercity slip | Sustain it (minutes, not hours); survive the response; outrun the Erosion bill | Every use is a career decision |
| T5 | Cataclysm | City-scale consequences; a single afternoon can redraw a map | Do it twice; do it secretly; survive the decade | ~40 alive; rarely past 50; every use is a geopolitical event |
| T6 | Worldtide | Continental consequences (three confirmed alive â€” CHAR-009/010/011 per Drafter A's registry: Okonkwo, Reyes, Shirakawa) | Anything without Compact observation; anything without dying by inches â€” all past 70 Fathoms | Living deterrents; the weapons that degrade themselves |
| T7 | Unknown | Reserved for "we don't know what that was" | Be confirmed (0 confirmed) | The designation exists because it has been needed |

> CANON: **Tier is not destiny in a fight.** Raw tier wins *unprepared* encounters. Preparation is the great equalizer â€” which is why intelligence, not output, is the true currency of the hidden world.

### What tier can't buy (hard limits, all tiers)

- **Time.** No tier alters the past ([02_WORLD_RULES.md](02_WORLD_RULES.md)). Causal bubbles (line-of-sight, minutes, ruinous Erosion) are the ceiling, and only some disciplines reach it.
- **Minds.** No tier performs direct mind control. A T6 Choir can steer a *crowd's* emotions; it cannot command an *individual's* obedience â€” suggestion seeding remains resistible, backlash-prone, and unreliable at every tier.
- **Permanence.** Borrowed matter reverts â‰¤72h at every tier. A T5 can build you a bridge; it cannot build you an empire.
- **Self.** No tier reverses Erosion â€” not even (especially not) on oneself. The healer's paradox: aggressive Bone healing *transfers* Erosion-risk to the healer.

## 30.2 Erosion economics per tier

> CANON: Output scales linearly; Erosion scales **exponentially past ~40 Fathoms**. The table below is the Compact medical directorate's actuarial summary â€” the numbers every handler, insurer, and general knows by heart.

| Tier | Typical cost per serious use | Sustainable career | What "one fight" costs | Life expectancy (active) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Negligible (<0.1 Fathom) | Decades; most never notice | Nothing | Normal |
| T2 | 0.5â€“2 Fathoms | 15â€“25 years of professional work at discipline hygiene | A bad week of migraines | Near-normal with care |
| T3 | 3â€“8 Fathoms | 8â€“15 years; the licensing tier exists because of this row | Months of recovery; visible thinning | Reduced; most retire by 55 |
| T4 | 10â€“25 Fathoms | 3â€“8 years at operational tempo; then desk, clinic, or Drowning | A year of self, minimum | Rarely past 60 active |
| T5 | 25â€“60 Fathoms | 1â€“3 major uses *total* past 60 Fathoms; the cruel arithmetic | Possibly everything | Rarely past 50 |
| T6 | 40+ Fathoms | Measured in *uses*, not years â€” all three confirmed are past 70 | The afternoon, and then the long dying | Dying by inches under observation |

**The three economic laws:**

1. **Peak output is cheap to buy and ruinous to use.** A T4 *can* level a building. The question their handler asks is never "can you" but "is the building worth a year of you."
2. **Endurance beats peak in every engagement longer than ninety seconds.** Conventional forces, wards, and prepared T2s win by *lasting* â€” the strong burn, the weak persist. This is why militaries still matter ([04_POWER_SYSTEM.md](04_POWER_SYSTEM.md)).
3. **Information is cheaper than Fathoms.** A Lantern T2 who knows a T4's Rule spends *zero* Fathoms to spoil a channeling worth 20. The entire hidden economy prices knowledge above output ([02_WORLD_RULES.md](02_WORLD_RULES.md)).

## 30.3 How the weak survive the strong

> CANON: Seven mechanisms. Every "weak defeats strong" scene in the novel must use at least one; the best use three.

**1. Rule interference.** Resonances interact through *conditions*, not power levels ([04_POWER_SYSTEM.md](04_POWER_SYSTEM.md)). Every ability has a Rule with requirements â€” line-of-sight, a name, a threshold, an exception clause. Attack the condition, not the channeler: break line-of-sight, flood the area with Tide-noise, trigger the exception. A T2 who has read the file beats a T4 who hasn't read the room.

**2. Preparation.** The strong improvise; the weak *prepare*. Wards take hours to raise and seconds to matter. Stillwater gas, Anchor restraints, documented Tide-marks, a building's blueprints, the target's schedule â€” preparation converts tier difference into a solved equation. The Compact's internal proverb: *"A T4 with a plan beats a T5 with a mood."*

**3. Terrain.** Thin places, warded zones, and mundane geography all favor the defender who chose them. A warded containment cell shreds unrecognized Slipping arrivals; a stairwell with a counting Rule eats the thirteenth pursuer regardless of tier. Home ground is a force multiplier the classification system doesn't measure.

**4. Tide-noise.** Artificial pressure static jams detection *and* channeling. Military-grade noise generators are the great equalizer of the modern battlefield (proven 2012, [EVENT-074](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)): a T0 squad with a jammer fights a T3 on nearly even terms for ninety seconds â€” and ninety seconds is usually enough.

**5. Information advantage.** Knowing the enemy's Rule, Fathom depth, handler, family, and schedule is worth more than two tiers. Lantern work, records work, *clerk* work â€” Arthur's whole survival strategy is this mechanism. The Ledger (INTL-003) prices it; the Red Ledger (SUP-004) auctions it.

**6. Erosion attrition.** The strong are on clocks; the weak are not. Every minute a T4 spends at full output is a minute off their life. Strategy: *don't win â€” last*. Make them spend. The Drowned leave Seeps; the patient inherit the field.

**7. Social and legal constraints.** The strong live in the world too. A T5 has a mother, a bank account, a Census file, a handler with a phone number. Choir use without a license is prison in 140+ countries; unregistered T3+ channeling is Seismograph-visible globally within minutes. The law is a leash the weak can pull â€” Arthur's documentation is meaningful precisely because the Tribunal (INTL-002) exists.

> CANON: These mechanisms are *why* the setting supports long-form storytelling without power escalation collapsing it. The ceiling is not "a bigger punch" â€” it is *a better-prepared nobody*.

## 30.4 Worked scenarios

### Scenario 1 â€” Prepared T2 vs arrogant T4 (the classic)
**Setup:** A T4 Tide debt-collector (67 Fathoms, accustomed to obedience) comes for a T2 Lantern archivist who has had three days' warning.
**The weak's play:** The archivist (a) floods her office with a commercial Tide-noise generator (mechanism 4), (b) breaks the Tide's line-of-sight Rule with a maze of bookshelves and a documented exception â€” the collector's Resonance requires *seeing* the target's hands (mechanism 1; she read his Tribunal file â€” mechanism 5), (c) fights from a warded reading room (mechanism 3).
**The strong's failure:** The collector burns 15 Fathoms in four minutes trying to force channeling through noise, hits nothing, and faces the arithmetic: one more push risks 80+ and pre-Drowning. He leaves. He will bill the client for the Fathoms.
**Lesson:** *Arrogance is an Erosion accelerant.* The T4 lost to paperwork.

### Scenario 2 â€” T0 Loud clerk vs T3 Choir interrogator
**Setup:** A licensed Choir T3 (corporate security) "interviews" a Loud records clerk about a leak. Direct mind control is impossible; suggestion seeding is the tool.
**The weak's play:** The clerk (a) *knows* he's being seeded â€” awareness is resistance ([02_WORLD_RULES.md](02_WORLD_RULES.md)); (b) writes everything down in real time, in triplicate, timestamps it â€” external memory the Choir cannot edit (mechanism 5 + 7); (c) reminds the interrogator, politely, that unlicensed Choir use is prison in 140+ countries and that *this interview is being logged by his union rep* (mechanism 7 â€” the licensed interrogator has more to lose).
**The strong's failure:** Seeding produces backlash â€” the interrogator leaves with a distorted echo of his own implanted impulse and a headache. The clerk leaves with notes.
**Lesson:** *Stubbornness is a countermeasure.* The file is armor.

### Scenario 3 â€” Sweeper team (T0s + one T1) vs a T4 Object Seep
**Setup:** "The Gilded Cradle" (ANOMALY-015, object/T4, per Drafter C's registry) â€” the Erosion-transfer Rule: an infant placed in the cradle sleeps one year and wakes carrying the rocker's transferred Fathoms; eleven uses, eleven children, and a Tribunal standing prohibition on a twelfth. A desperate T4 (71 Fathoms, six months from Drowning) has stolen a *twelfth* infant and is rocking the cradle in a Jakarta apartment block.
**The weak's play:** The Sweepers don't fight the object â€” they fight its *Rule*. (a) The Tribunal prohibition order makes the *use* the crime â€” secure the perimeter and invoke the order by radio before entering (legal mechanism; the rocker is now committing a Tribunal offense, not a rescue); (b) the Rule needs an infant *placed* and a rocker who *sleeps the full hour and wakes* â€” deny the placement: evacuate the infant's family first, so there is no second placement if the first is interrupted (mechanism 1); (c) the transfer completes only when the rocker *wakes* â€” interrupt the rocking before the hour completes: cut power, flood the flat with light and noise, drag the rocker out mid-sleep (mechanism 2+3); (d) document the Rule for the Tribunal's containment desk â€” the interrupted twelfth use is the evidence the prohibition order needs for renewal.
**Outcome:** Zero casualties, one contained object, one arrested rocker, one infant who never slept. A very boring after-action report. Sweepers consider boring reports the highest art.
**Lesson:** *The exterminator model.* Professionals don't duel anomalies; they process them. The Tribunal's prohibition order is a weapon the Sweepers can pick up and use.

### Scenario 4 â€” T5 vs a city (why the T5 loses)
**Setup:** A grieving T5 Tide (88 Fathoms) decides a city's government will answer for a coverup. Maximum output, no restraint.
**What happens:** Minute 0â€“3: catastrophic local effects; the Seismograph network lights up globally. Minute 3â€“10: the Joint Containment Command (INTL-006) declares; Tide-noise saturation begins; Drowndust munitions are authorized (banned, stockpiled, used â€” [EVENT-083](25_TIMEmessaging app.md) is the precedent everyone pretends isn't). Minute 10â€“30: the T5's Erosion curve goes vertical â€” 88 to 100 is *one afternoon* at maximum output. The city survives because it is *large* and *patient*; the T5 Drowns, usually before the army even arrives, leaving a new Seep the Sweepers will process by Thursday.
**The deeper loss:** The T5's family lived in that city. Their Census file is now a memorial. Social constraints (mechanism 7) are why this scenario is rare â€” the strong know the arithmetic.
**Lesson:** *A T5 can't fight long.* Endurance beats peak; the city is the ultimate weak survivor.

### Scenario 5 â€” Arthur (T0, Loud, Laggard) vs a T2 Hollow tracker
**Setup:** A Cartographer-contracted T2 Hollow is paid to follow Arthur and report his routine. Hollow tracking: reading his "wake" through thin places.
**The weak's play:** Arthur (a) has read the tracker's discipline from NQA files â€” Hollow tracking needs *his wake*, which the Laggard *eats* (the tether drinks ambient information; his wake is 3 seconds stale and wrong â€” mechanism 1, accidental); (b) prepares terrain: he walks his route through a warded old-quarter in Ravenhurst, where unrecognized Hollow work shreds (mechanism 3); (c) when cornered, steps into the lag â€” 3 seconds out-of-phase, unseen â€” and simply *leaves* (mechanism: the anomaly, Â§B.11 use 5).
**The strong's failure:** The tracker reports that the target "has no wake" â€” and bills for a wasted week. She never sees the shadow step.
**Lesson:** *The Laggard's weakness is camouflage.* Being filed T1 is the best ward Arthur owns.

### Scenario 6 â€” T4 vs a corporation (the foreclosure)
**Setup:** A T4 Bone enforcer decides Halcyon Dynamics (CORP-001) owes him a debt. He can win any fight in the building.
**The corporation's play:** Halcyon doesn't fight. It (a) freezes his accounts via Ledger (INTL-003) compliance flags (mechanism 7); (b) leaks his Census file and Fathom depth to the Tribunal's press desk â€” *registered, 71 Fathoms, unlicensed Bone augmentation* (mechanism 5+7); (c) offers his handler a better contract; (d) waits. The enforcer can win any *fight*. There is no fight. There is paperwork, and then there is a cell.
**Lesson:** *Institutions are the apex predator of individuals.* Erosion kills the strong; bureaucracy buries them.

# 31 â€” CONFLICT ENGINE: 52 Reusable Generators

> CANON: Conflicts in this setting are structural, not villain-driven. Each generator below is a *machine* â€” it recurs because the incentives recur. Every entry gives: setup, factions (registry IDs), why it recurs, 2â€“3 escalation paths, and what **Arthur** â€” weak, clever, Loud, a clerk â€” can do in it. His moves are never "win the fight"; they are *read the file, find the Rule, spend someone else's strength*.

### CG-001 â€” The Delinquent Claim
- **Setup:** A Quiet-policy claim crosses Arthur's desk: the incident described is impossible, the claimant is Loud, and someone has already paid it â€” twice, under two names.
- **Factions:** CORP-011 (NQA), CRIM-002 (Naga Hitam), INTL-003 (the Ledger).
- **Why it recurs:** Insurance fraud with Seeps is the perfect crime â€” the Veil eats the witnesses and static rot eats the evidence.
- **Escalation:** 1) The double-paid claimant Drowns mid-investigation, leaving a Seep in a claims office. 2) The fraud maps onto a Naga Hitam laundering pipeline (cf. CASE-006, the Surabaya litigation). 3) The Ledger opens a misclassification case and subpoenas Arthur's files.
- **Arthur's angle:** He is the only person who remembers both versions of the claim. Cross-referencing is a superpower here â€” and a target on his back.

### CG-002 â€” The Sweeper's Bad Night
- **Setup:** A routine cleanup goes wrong: the Seep's Rule was misfiled, the ward fails, and a Sweeper team is trapped inside with civilians.
- **Factions:** GOV-006 (SMD), CHAR-034 (Aisha Rahman), IND-004 (Night Clerks).
- **Why it recurs:** 96% of Seeps are T0â€“T2 until the 4% that aren't; misclassification is a statistical certainty at scale.
- **Escalation:** 1) The team must be extracted by breaking the Rule's exception clause â€” which nobody documented. 2) A civilian films it; the 180-second livestream rule ([EVENT-080](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)) starts ticking. 3) The team's handler orders a Drowndust option nobody will admit to afterward.
- **Arthur's angle:** He filed the original incident report. His memory of the *first* telling â€” before the file was "corrected" â€” contains the exception clause.

### CG-003 â€” The Census Knock
- **Setup:** BPF canvassers come for a voluntary Census interview; the interviewee is an unregistered T3 hiding in plain sight as a street-food vendor.
- **Factions:** GOV-004, the vendor's family, SUP-009 (Pale Court, watching bloodlines).
- **Why it recurs:** Registration is voluntary in Indonesia, mandatory nowhere comfortably; every Census drive finds someone.
- **Escalation:** 1) The vendor panics and channels â€” Seismograph-visible in minutes. 2) The Pale Court offers "protection" (a leash with better catering). 3) The canvassers are Night Clerks sympathizers and look the other way â€” now they're compromised too.
- **Arthur's angle:** He knows the vendor (warung regular). He can warn, hide paperwork, or â€” hardest â€” convince a frightened T3 that the file is safer than the street.

### CG-004 â€” The Gray Market Double-Cross
- **Setup:** A Red Ledger-escrowed deal in Trieste (CITY-020): the seller's *Rule documentation* is forged, the object is real, and the buyer's money is Drowndust-adjacent.
- **Factions:** SUP-004 (Red Ledger), CRIM-001 (Koi Network), CHAR-027 (the Factor).
- **Why it recurs:** Anomalies are non-fungible ([02_WORLD_RULES.md](02_WORLD_RULES.md)) â€” every deal is bespoke, every deal is a trust fall.
- **Escalation:** 1) The forged Rule gets someone killed; the Ledger's escrow guarantee is invoked â€” in blood. 2) The Koi Network steals the real documentation mid-transfer (their signature). 3) Three governments' buyers realize they bid on the same lot.
- **Arthur's angle:** None directly â€” until the forged documentation turns out to be *his* NQA claim file with the serials filed off. Then it's his problem.

### CG-005 â€” The Choir in the Office
- **Setup:** A mid-level manager at a Jakarta firm is an unlicensed T2 Choir; turnover is zero, morale is "excellent," and two employees have filed Quiet claims for "dreams about work."
- **Factions:** CORP-011 (the claims), GOV-004 (unlicensed Choir = prison), the manager.
- **Why it recurs:** Choir is the most useful and most regulated discipline; every year someone decides the license is optional.
- **Escalation:** 1) The seeding escalates â€” employees start "volunteering" for dangerous overtime. 2) A licensed Choir auditor is sent; auditor vs. rogue becomes a seeding duel with the staff as the field. 3) Backlash: the manager starts experiencing his own implanted impulses.
- **Arthur's angle:** He's Loud â€” the seeding slides off him, which makes him the only reliable witness. His notes become the auditor's case file. The manager notices the one employee who never smiles at the right time.

### CG-006 â€” The Infohazard Sermon
- **Setup:** A Ninth Bell street preacher (SUP-007) is preaching from a text that *propagates* â€” an Information Seep; listeners leave Loud about the wrong things.
- **Factions:** SUP-007/REL-006, GOV-004, IND-001 (Static Hour podcast â€” they want to record it).
- **Why it recurs:** Information Seeps can't be put in vaults; they ride the cheapest medium available, which is currently a human voice.
- **Escalation:** 1) The sermon goes viral as a "creepy TikTok" â€” the 2017 protocols vs. algorithmic spread. 2) The text mutates in retelling (Seeps evolve under attention). 3) The preacher is sincere, Loud, not Attuned â€” Amos Kade's (CHAR-030) people are watching to recruit him.
- **Arthur's angle:** He can listen *safely-ish* â€” Loud, careful, taking notes â€” and transcribe the Rule. Transcription is containment's first step. It's also how infohazards get *him*.

### CG-007 â€” The Drowndust Cache
- **Setup:** A construction crew in North Jakarta digs up a sealed crate: military markings, no manifest, and the foreman's nose won't stop bleeding.
- **Factions:** CRIM-002, GOV-003 (the likely source), INTL-002 (the Tribunal's sealed Kyiv case).
- **Why it recurs:** Four states stockpiled what the Accords banned; stockpiles leak, get sold, get buried, get found.
- **Escalation:** 1) Naga Hitam tries to sell it; the buyers are BPF stingers. 2) The crate's contents are *spent* Drowndust â€” inert, but the paperwork isn't, and the paperwork names names. 3) Someone uses it â€” Erosion as a weapon, the war crime nobody prosecutes.
- **Arthur's angle:** The crate's shipping labels route through an NQA-insured logistics firm. His files know where the crate has been. Paper trails are his native terrain.

### CG-008 â€” The Inheritance
- **Setup:** A Pale Court dynast dies; the will leaves an Object Seep to three heirs, one of whom is Quiet and must never know what it is.
- **Factions:** SUP-009, INTL-003 (Ledger arbitration â€” cf. CASE-004, *In re: The Widow's Teacup*), the Quiet heir's family.
- **Why it recurs:** Dynasties are fragile ([04_POWER_SYSTEM.md](04_POWER_SYSTEM.md)) â€” every generation must survive its First Tide, and estates don't.
- **Escalation:** 1) The Quiet heir activates it by accident. 2) The Attuned heirs contest the will via Tribunal â€” depth-adjusted sentencing looms. 3) Vivienne Ashworth (CHAR-025) intervenes personally; her interventions are never free.
- **Arthur's angle:** The estate's Quiet insurer is NQA. Arthur processes the claim â€” and notices the will's codicil describes *his* anomaly's filing number. The Court has been watching longer than he knew.

### CG-009 â€” The Lantern's Price
- **Setup:** A freelance T2 Lantern sells Tide-mark readings to divorce lawyers, journalists, and one crime syndicate â€” until a reading shows her *own* client's murder, scheduled.
- **Factions:** IND-005 (Pro Bono Lanterns), CRIM-002, GOV-004.
- **Why it recurs:** Lantern is the lightest-regulated discipline and the most monetizable; the market always finds the unlicensed.
- **Escalation:** 1) She sells the warning; the client pays the syndicate instead. 2) She withholds it; the murder happens on her conscience and in her Tide-marks. 3) The syndicate decides the Lantern herself is the loose end â€” and hires a counter-Lantern.
- **Arthur's angle:** Kirana (CHAR-033) brings him the case â€” a Quiet-care counselor's ethics vs. a clerk's documentation. Arthur's job: make the unreadable *filed* â€” a record the syndicate can't Veil away.

### CG-010 â€” The Quiet Garden's Offer
- **Setup:** The Quiet Garden (SUP-003/REL-007) invites Arthur to a Stillness retreat â€” no recruitment pitch, just "your shadow is tired."
- **Factions:** SUP-003, GOV-004 (watches the Garden warily), CHAR-018's memory (Yusuf once visited; his logbook says "they were kind, I was afraid").
- **Why it recurs:** The Garden collects the weary; the hidden world manufactures the weary at scale.
- **Escalation:** 1) The Stillness practices *work* on the lag â€” it shortens, for the first time in anyone's records â€” and something at the other end *notices the quiet*. 2) BPF reads the retreat as defection. 3) The Garden asks its price: not his service â€” his *journals*, for their archive.
- **Arthur's angle:** He wants the training and fears the vow. The Garden's price is always the same: *stay*. His mother needs him home for Lebaran.

### CG-011 â€” The Erosion Ward
- **Setup:** Ward 7, RS Kencana (MED-001) â€” Jakarta's Quiet-care ward â€” admits a 19-year-old T3 at 74 Fathoms who doesn't want treatment; she wants *one more job*.
- **Factions:** MED-001 staff, CORP-002 (Vesper â€” her file is flagged), her crew.
- **Why it recurs:** Erosion is terminal and irreversible; every ward has a patient doing the arithmetic out loud.
- **Escalation:** 1) She walks out; the Holloway Breach ([EVENT-078](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)) is the staff's nightmare reference. 2) Vesper offers an experimental protocol â€” consent, or coercion with better lighting. 3) Her "one more job" is a hit on someone Arthur knows.
- **Arthur's angle:** Hannah (CHAR-012) nurses at Cipto, not Kencana â€” but the wards talk. Arthur's angle is information: her file crosses his desk, and what's *missing* from it matters more than what's there.

### CG-012 â€” The Cartographer's Commission
- **Setup:** Pramudya Nugroho (CHAR-032) offers Arthur a deal: let the Exchange *map* the Laggard â€” non-invasive, well-paid, historic â€” and they'll give him Ilsa Brandt's journals.
- **Factions:** SUP-002, CORP-011 (his employer would fire him for moonlighting with anomalies), CHAR-019's ghost.
- **Why it recurs:** The Cartographers map everything; the unmappable is their professional obsession.
- **Escalation:** 1) The mapping is *not* non-invasive â€” the tether reacts to being surveyed. 2) The journals contain Ilsa's last-page warning, and Pram hasn't read that far. 3) The Exchange's buyer for the survey data is the Red Ledger.
- **Arthur's angle:** He wants the journals more than the money. The negotiation â€” what he trades, what he withholds â€” is the whole conflict. Clerks negotiate with files.

### CG-013 â€” The Rememberers' Meeting
- **Setup:** The Rememberers (IND-002), a Loud support group, invite Arthur to speak â€” and one member's "memory" is a Tide-mark bleed that never happened to anyone.
- **Factions:** IND-002, IND-004 (Night Clerks â€” overlap), GOV-004 (monitors both, lightly).
- **Why it recurs:** Loud people need each other; shared memory is the only community the Veil can't dissolve.
- **Escalation:** 1) The false memory is *contagious* â€” an Information Seep riding the support group. 2) A BPF monitor decides the group is a cult-in-formation. 3) The member with the false memory is being seeded â€” by whom, and why a support group?
- **Arthur's angle:** His recall is perfect; he can *prove* the memory is false. Proving it means calling a vulnerable person a liar in the one room they felt safe. His hardest conflicts are never about monsters.

### CG-014 â€” The Halcyon Audit
- **Setup:** Halcyon Dynamics (CORP-001) hires NQA to audit its "luck" â€” three quarters of impossible positioning, and its Quiet-compliance officer just Drowned.
- **Factions:** CORP-001, CORP-011, INTL-003 (Ledger compliance).
- **Why it recurs:** Corporate precognition is the oldest financial crime in the hidden world; the analysts always Drown eventually.
- **Escalation:** 1) The audit finds the precognition desk is still running â€” on borrowed analysts. 2) The Ledger moves to delist Halcyon's Quiet paper; the market panics. 3) The Drowned officer left a Seep in the risk department.
- **Arthur's angle:** He's on the audit team as the records man. He finds the pattern in the trade timestamps â€” and realizes the desk's "luck" has been *watching him back* through the files.

### CG-015 â€” The Koi Network's Debt
- **Setup:** The Koi Network (CRIM-001) decides Arthur's Night Clerks thread owes them for a warning they never asked for â€” payable in information.
- **Factions:** CRIM-001, IND-004, CRIM-002 (Naga Hitam â€” rival claim on the same debt).
- **Why it recurs:** Criminal information economies run on invented obligations; the Gray Market invented the invoice.
- **Escalation:** 1) The "debt" is sold to Naga Hitam, who collect differently. 2) The information they want is a Sweeper patrol schedule â€” Arthur doesn't have it, but Aisha's (CHAR-034) SMD-contracted team does. 3) Refusal means the Night Clerks get named to the SMD as an unlicensed Loud assembly.
- **Arthur's angle:** He negotiates with the one thing criminals undervalue: *accurate paperwork*. A clean ledger of what was actually owed, filed where it can't be Veil-edited.

### CG-016 â€” The Vatican Asylum
- **Setup:** A sapient organism Seep washes up in disputed waters; the Vatican's OEP (GOV-010) invokes the Asylum Protocol â€” the Sulu precedent ([EVENT-073](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)).
- **Factions:** GOV-010, INTL-001, COUNTRY-004/COUNTRY-025 navies, SUP-008 (the Archivists want its testimony â€” it's *old*).
- **Why it recurs:** The sea keeps delivering; jurisdiction keeps failing; the Protocol is the only law that fits.
- **Escalation:** 1) Two navies arrive first; the organism chooses none of them. 2) It speaks â€” in 14th-century Venetian â€” and the Archivists go pale. 3) Someone decides asylum is cheaper to prevent than to grant.
- **Arthur's angle:** Distant â€” until NQA is asked to insure the asylum transport. Arthur files the policy. The policy's incident history includes the *first* asylum case, and its Tide-marks don't match the official story.

### CG-017 â€” The Static Hour Episode
- **Setup:** The Static Hour podcast (IND-001) wants Arthur as an anonymous source â€” "the clerk who remembers." They offer him a voice modulator and a big audience.
- **Factions:** IND-001, CORP-006 (Pale Lantern â€” noise farmers who'd love to *own* the episode), GOV-004.
- **Why it recurs:** Every Loud person eventually wants to *tell*; the masquerade runs on that wanting being managed.
- **Escalation:** 1) The episode airs; static rot eats the "proof" segments but not Arthur's voice. 2) Pale Lantern buys the podcast â€” the tell becomes content. 3) A listener starts mapping the modulator's artifacts â€” the voice is *local*, and the net tightens on Ravenhurst's night shift.
- **Arthur's angle:** He says no â€” and the episode airs anyway, with someone else's voice where his would have been. Arthur's conflict is the aftermath: the tell happened without him, and he knows exactly what telling costs.

### CG-018 â€” The Drowned Choir's Baptism
- **Setup:** The Choir (SUP-001) announces a public baptism in Jakarta â€” and their "holy water" is Chapel-of-the-Deep water, a genuine Place Seep in liquid form.
- **Factions:** SUP-001/REL-005, GOV-004, REL-003 (Majelis Fenomena â€” the Islamic scholars' working group, furious).
- **Why it recurs:** The Choir's theology requires *witnesses*; Drowning is their sacrament and their recruitment.
- **Escalation:** 1) The baptism works â€” attendees emerge Loud, weeping, converted. 2) Majelis Fenomena issues a ruling; the streets take sides. 3) One baptized attendee Drowns within the month â€” the Choir calls it ascension; the family calls it murder.
- **Arthur's angle:** The Choir wants *him* â€” the shadow-blessed â€” as their witness. His refusal must be public enough to stick and quiet enough to survive. His mother is in the crowd.

### CG-019 â€” The Hollow Man's Request
- **Setup:** Silas Crane (CHAR-029), 82 Fathoms, asks Arthur for a favor: *sit with me while I sleep.* "Something stands in the shallow places. Yours might know its name."
- **Factions:** SUP-006, RES-005 (Holloway â€” Crane's ward), the thing at the other end of the tether.
- **Why it recurs:** The pre-Drowning need witnesses; the living need warnings; neither gets what they want.
- **Escalation:** 1) Crane Drowns mid-watch â€” and the tether *reacts*; the lag spikes to minutes. 2) What Crane saw, he wrote down; the note is in Arthur's pocket now. 3) The Hollow Men come to collect Crane's effects â€” and notice Arthur.
- **Arthur's angle:** He says yes, because clerks don't abandon the night shift. He learns what the shadow looks like from the *other* side â€” through a dying man's description. It costs him sleep for a month.

### CG-020 â€” The Night Shift War
- **Setup:** NQA's night shift is being hollowed out â€” reassigned, retired early, replaced by a "records automation" system that misfiles Seep claims at a rate that can't be accidental.
- **Factions:** CORP-011 management, IND-004 (the Night Clerks are all night-shift), an unknown saboteur.
- **Why it recurs:** The hidden world runs on night labor; night labor is the first budget cut and the first compromised.
- **Escalation:** 1) The automation is *eating* claims â€” specifically claims with Arthur's initials on them. 2) The saboteur is the Lantern-screened HR officer who approved Arthur's hiring. 3) The misfiled claims form a pattern: someone is *curating* what gets remembered.
- **Arthur's angle:** His home turf. He knows the filing system better than the saboteur. This is the conflict he was born for â€” and winning it means exposing who wanted him hired.

### CG-021 â€” The Pale Court's Proposal
- **Setup:** Vivienne Ashworth (CHAR-025) invites the Reed family to dinner â€” all of them, including Eleanor â€” her supermarket shifts permitting. The proposal: a Court stipend, a London education for "the boy," and discretion about the shadow.
- **Factions:** SUP-009, the Reed family (CHAR-012/013/014), GOV-004 (watches the Court's bloodline collecting with alarm).
- **Why it recurs:** Dynasties need fresh bloodlines; Loud lines are the rarest asset; the Court has been acquiring for centuries.
- **Escalation:** 1) Hannah (CHAR-012) is tempted â€” the stipend would change everything. 2) The Court's genealogist finds something in the Reed line â€” a Hollow Pattern carrier three generations back, unawakened. 3) Refusal has a price; the Court always collects *something*.
- **Arthur's angle:** He can't fight the Court. He can *read the offer* â€” the contract's Quiet clauses, the filed precedents (cf. CASE-004) â€” and find the clause that lets his family walk away. Clerks read contracts.

### CG-022 â€” The Vesper Study
- **Setup:** Dr. Amara Nwosu (CHAR-031) offers Arthur a fully-funded, fully-consensual longitudinal study: quarterly scans, generous stipend, publication credit. All she wants is to *watch* the Laggard for ten years.
- **Factions:** CORP-002, INTL-001 science directorate (which suppressed her paper), Arthur's caution.
- **Why it recurs:** Science needs subjects; the hidden world needs science; consent is the battlefield.
- **Escalation:** 1) The scans show the ratchet is *accelerating* â€” 3.1s and climbing. 2) Vesper's board wants the study's *real* product: a zero-Erosion channeling model. 3) Nwosu's suppressed paper leaks â€” with Arthur's anonymized data recognizable to anyone who knows him.
- **Arthur's angle:** He wants to know what he is. The study is the only honest offer he's had. Honesty, in this world, is the most expensive thing on the menu.

### CG-023 â€” The Sweeper's Choice
- **Setup:** Aisha Rahman's (CHAR-034) team corners a T3 who's been seeding a school â€” and the T3 is fourteen, terrified, and at 61 Fathoms.
- **Factions:** GOV-014, the child's family, INTL-002 (Tribunal â€” depth-adjusted sentencing for minors is untested).
- **Why it recurs:** Awakening needs trauma; trauma keeps happening to children; the system keeps arriving late.
- **Escalation:** 1) The child channels during containment â€” Seismograph-visible, and the JCC wants jurisdiction. 2) The parents choose the Pale Court's "protection" over the ward. 3) Aisha breaks protocol â€” and Arthur is the only witness who *can't* be Veil-edited into forgetting she did.
- **Arthur's angle:** He documents what actually happened. Documentation is testimony; testimony is the difference between a broken rule and a buried one. This is where the romance thread and the duty thread collide.

### CG-024 â€” The Ferrymen's Toll
- **Setup:** The Ferrymen (SUP-010) â€” who move things that can't be moved legally â€” lose a shipment in Jakarta: an Object Seep, T3, Rule unknown, last seen in a Styx Logistics (CORP-007) container Arthur's files insured.
- **Factions:** SUP-010, CORP-007, CRIM-005 (the Salt Road wants the route back).
- **Why it recurs:** The hidden world has logistics; logistics have losses; losses have Rules.
- **Escalation:** 1) The object's Rule activates in the container yard â€” the yard starts *keeping* things. 2) The Ferrymen's client is Department 12 (GOV-003). 3) The insurance claim lands on Arthur's desk, and the object's description matches a file his office "never had."
- **Arthur's angle:** Follow the paperwork. The container's manifest, the policy's riders, the yard's tide tables â€” the object is findable by *bureaucracy*, which is Arthur's element.

### CG-025 â€” The Marked Ministry Crusade
- **Setup:** The Marked Ministry (REL-002) launches a "deliverance" campaign in Ravenhurst's Willowmere high street â€” targeting, among others, a supermarket part-timer's son "followed by a shadow" since the 2018 incident his mother still won't discuss.
- **Factions:** REL-002, the Willowmere shopkeepers' association (embarrassed), the Reed family, GOV-006 (hates street-level supernatural politics).
- **Why it recurs:** Folk demonology meets real phenomena; the Ministry is wrong about the theology and right that *something* is there.
- **Escalation:** 1) The campaign draws a crowd â€” crowds amplify (the Mainz lesson, [EVENT-002](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)). 2) A genuine Seep rides the revival's attention. 3) Eleanor must choose, publicly, between her neighbors and her son.
- **Arthur's angle:** He can't debunk them without exposing himself. He protects his mother the only way he can: by making the campaign's *paperwork* fail â€” permits, noise ordinances, the quiet machinery of the city.

### CG-026 â€” The Tribunal Subpoena
- **Setup:** The Tribunal (INTL-002) subpoenas Arthur as a witness in the sealed Kyiv Drowndust case ([EVENT-083](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)) â€” his NQA files contain the shipping records.

- **Arthur's angle:** Tell the truth, completely, on the record â€” and live with who hears it. The clerk's ultimate move: *filing the truth where it can't be unfiled*.

- **Escalation:** 1) ROT/FEED stakes out the intersection for a re-occurrence â€” livestreaming it. 2) The 180-second rule fails; the stream survives because the *fake* framing protects it. 3) The Seep escalates under a million viewers' attention.

The transfer is the beat: the absorption is why the Quiet Desk has it, and why Aisha's unfiled BPF follow-ups read as treason to the agency that now owns the case.

### CG-052 â€” The High Tide Contingency
- **Setup:** The Compact's High Tide Contingency ([EVENT-090](25_TIMEmessaging app.md)) leaks â€” in outline: triage lists, which cities get Sweepers, which get *abandoned*, and the "post-secrecy" protocols for a world where everyone knows.

The city learns this. 2) Factions activate their private contingencies â€” the Choir's baptisms, the Court's arks, the Ledger's auctions of *escape*. 3) Arthur must decide what his files are *for* â€” evidence, leverage, or a lifeboat.
- **Arthur's angle:** Everything he is converges here: the perfect witness, the clerk's archive, the Laggard's window, the clean recording. In the post-secrecy world, *proof* is the only currency â€” and he is the only mint. The final escalation is his choice: **spend the masquerade to save the city, or keep the secret and watch the triage list execute.** The novel earns this decision over hundreds of chapters. This generator is the engine's redline â€” use sparingly, and mean it.
